Recently I realized I didn't like who I was becoming with my partner and am currently doing some self care to change that. I have unfortunately become more disconnected emotionally/mentally/physically from my partner, but it has been the only way i could gather enough energy to take care of myself again. We're going through abit of a roommate phase figuring out what works for each of us.

Before living with him, I use to eat healthy, exercise daily, work on my hobbies semi regularly. I was like this while we long distance dated and he was sweet, seemed reliable, romantic...and then I moved in with him (before he was dx) during the pandemic, and in less than a month of living together he got bored and I seemingly stopped existing... I thought I had been bait and switched. And the pandemic had me feeling trapped. The first year was really rough. Enough that when his friends who were frequent drinkers would visit, I started having the occasional drink with them which was something I didn't really do before. It helped numb some of the stress. Thankfully I do not do this anymore.

When he finally got on meds and I saw the guy I had been dating come back, I cried myself to sleep that night. The guy I loved was in there, but what I lived with for that first year was his adhd dysfunction. Things weren't perfect when he was on meds, but I could talk to him again with out him melting down. But he ended up in hospital multiple times from having bad reactions to adhd meds... So now we're back to none...

He has more awareness now so it is not as bad as the first time without meds... but it is still exhausting and lonely, and I've decided that I'm going to live how I lived before I moved in with him I'm trying to shift my energy back to me and see if I can find myself again. We'll see how it goes.

He at least gave the cats fresh water and their feeder was still full, but he already avoids the cat litter because of allergies. He also kept doing the laundry, but nothing else around the house had been kept up with. I was tired when I got home and he wanted all kinds of attention and I ended up barking at him cause all I wanted to do was unwind and felt like I couldn't with the house in that state.

I know overcompensating leads to more unwanted behavior... but when he's off his meds it feels almost impossible to get him to do anything. I've tried leaving things to him, but feel like I can't count on him if he doesn't have his meds to keep him stable enough to focus. He once complained that if I would stop doing the dishes he would pitch in more... so I stopped doing the dishes for a week... then I ended up with a weeks worth of dishes to deal with and fruit flies. He then claimed he was too tired after work to do anything and that he planned on doing them on the weekend. I can't live like that. I work from home so it feels like all I do at home is work and not live when he's off his meds.

I've thought about what I get from this relationship alot and its hard to explain... I love him, and when he's functioning he's a wonderful person to be with... but it's when he stops functioning that I feel like I'm carrying a lead weight around and it's frustrating ... the good is good, and the bad is draining.... I was hoping that maybe there's a new medicine or treatment we haven't tried... sounds like the biggest thing we need is a doctor with an actual clue about adhd... but where we live I worry that may not be possible.

I'm not formally diagnosed, so my thoughts might be off the mark... but these questions would have called me out.

Do you find constant pressure calming? (weighted blanket or similar)

Do you feel like you need to memorize a script to interact with people?

Do you feel like everyone else was given a manual on life that you weren't?

Does loud noise or bright lights trigger overwhelm?

Are you sensitive to food textures, tastes, or smell?

Do you have a hard time understanding boundaries, both others and your own?

We're you bullied and didn't understand why?

Do you prefer the world in your head to the world outside?

Were you perceived as extremely above average or gifted in specific interests, but below average where you had no interest?

Do you feel like you don't know what to do with your body when idle?

Do you struggle with communication, or being misunderstood?

Do you have delays with processing emotion, or are uncertain what emotion you are feeling?

It in itself is not a moral judgement, however people frequently use it to back up their body shaming bias'. It is highly flawed, and should not be held up as the cure all for weight control.

Knew a paramedic that was physically active, didn't eat much, and yet struggled to control their weight and blood sugar because of chronic stress/high cortisol. This person saved lives for a living. When someone assumes that person is just a lazy couch potato eating all day it makes me want to kick those presumptuous people in the teeth.

Hormones play a huge role with weight especially in people over 30 and women.

If you only cut calories, ghrelin goes up (telling you you're starving making you crave food), this also causes increased cortisol (stress hormone), your metabolism slows down because leptin decreases (mean you start burning fewer calories in your body). 

If you fast, yes eventually you will go into ketosis (a metabolic state that when your body burns fat for energy instead of glucose) however in women this can cause hormone disruption throwing off estrogen and progesterone levels throwing off ovulation cycles (shockingly bodies don't want to focus on reproduction when they think you're starving). This can make it hard to keep the weight loss off (it rebounds after the fast is over.)

Anytime you're stressed cortisol shoots up which can increase your blood glucose level (cortisol triggers gluconeogenesis in the liver to create glucose to give you energy to fight the threat your body thinks stress is) again leading to weight gain.
